title: Rabbi Bana’ah the Early
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Berakhot 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.55b.16), Rabbi Bizna cites Rabbi Akiva, who cites Rabbi Panda in Rabbi Nachum’s name. Rabbi Nachum cites Rabbi Birim in the name of an elder identified as Rabbi Bana’ah: “There were twenty-four dream interpreters in Jerusalem. Once I dreamed a dream and went to all of them,” etc. Hyman considers this Rabbi Bana’ah undoubtedly early, when Israel was still in Jerusalem. Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads: “Rabbi Parna said in the name of an elder — and who is he? Rabbi Nehorai.” Hyman considers the word Nehora’ah very easily confused with the name Bana’ah.

notes.text: Undoubtedly retains Hyman’s asserted strength, while the proposed early dating and Nehorai/Bana’ah letter confusion remain attributed to him.

The consulted [Berakhot 55b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.55b.16) names Rabbi Bana’ah at the end of this chain. Hyman separately reports a reading that names Rabbi Nehorai and offers his own explanation of the difference.
